nodes.name: Website Lead
nodes.notes:
Header auth, not "open webhook plus a check in a Code node". An unauthenticated
endpoint that validates later still executes the workflow for every request,
which is a free denial-of-service and a free way to fill the audit log.

nodes.name: WhatsApp Inbound
nodes.notes:
Accepts the real WhatsApp Business Cloud API envelope
(entry[].changes[].value.messages[]) and a flat {from,name,text} shape for
testing. Going live against Meta is a URL swap plus their signature header;
nothing downstream changes.

Meta retries an unacknowledged webhook for up to 7 days, which is precisely why
the response is sent before the processing rather than after it.

nodes.name: Parse CSV Batch
nodes.notes:
Uses I.parseCsv from _shared/intake.js: quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded
commas and newlines, CRLF and a BOM. A split(",") import corrupts data silently,
which is worse than failing, because nobody looks.

nodes.name: Read Intake Ledger
nodes.notes:
Filtered per item, so a 50-row import does 50 keyed lookups rather than one
full-table scan. Verified live with a multi-row batch before it was trusted -
see 05_Test_Evidence.

continueRegularOutput here is a considered exception, not a habit: this node is
NOT on the path to the webhook response (that branches earlier), and a ledger
read that fails should degrade to "assume nothing was seen before" - a possible
duplicate - rather than reject a real lead outright. Losing a lead is worse than
processing one twice, and everything downstream is idempotent anyway.

nodes.name: Respond Accepted
nodes.notes:
202 Accepted, deliberately, and sent BEFORE the handoff. The lead has been
durably claimed by this point but not yet qualified, and 202 is the honest code
for that. It also stops WhatsApp retrying: Meta re-delivers anything it does not
see acknowledged quickly, for up to seven days.

The body names every outcome - accepted, duplicate, quarantined, ignored, plus
the lead_uids - so the caller and the edge-case runner can assert on it instead
of inferring success from a bare 200.

nodes.name: Write Intake Audit

value.detail_json: ={{ JSON.stringify({ detail: $json.audit_detail, source: $json.source, source_ref: $json.source_ref || "", idem_key: $json.idem_key || "", batch_id: $json.batch_id || "", line: $json.line || 0 }) }}

nodes.notes:
Every arrival is logged, including the ones that go nowhere. n8n's own
execution log is not an audit trail: it is pruned on a schedule and it cannot be
queried by lead. "What happened to lead X" has to be answerable from a table.

A failed audit write must not fail the intake, hence continueRegularOutput -
and this node is a leaf, so nothing downstream inherits a broken item.

nodes.name: Route Intake
nodes.notes:
No fallback output on purpose. "duplicate" and "ignored" are terminal states
whose only required action - the audit row - already happened on branch 2. An
explicit dead end is clearer than a NoOp node that exists to look tidy.

nodes.name: Claim Intake
nodes.notes:
Claim BEFORE the handoff, never after. A crash between the two leaves a row in
state="claimed" with no completion, which is exactly the signal the reconciler
in LP-03 looks for: it searches Odoo by the external key, finds whether the work
actually happened, and either finishes the ledger or re-runs it. That is edge
case 7 handled by a mechanism instead of by hoping.

nodes.name: Store Lead
nodes.notes:
Upsert, not insert. lead_uid is derived from the idempotency key, so a replay
of the same delivery rewrites the same row rather than creating a second one -
the record is durable before LP-02 is even asked to run.

budget_band and urgency are carried in the payload to LP-02 rather than stored
here: the Data Table schema is immutable through the API, so every speculative
column is permanent. They belong to the score, and the score is stored as its
breakdown.

nodes.name: Handoff to Qualify
nodes.notes:
mode "each": one LP-02 execution per lead, so a single poisonous row in a
50-row import cannot take the other 49 down with it. One failed execution, 49
successes, one dead letter.

waitForSubWorkflow false: intake is done once the lead is claimed and stored.
Blocking here would put enrichment, an AI call and an Odoo round trip inside the
webhook window, which is how a source starts retrying and one lead becomes four.

The whole payload crosses as ONE JSON STRING. Sub-workflow inputs flatten nested
objects unpredictably (the same lesson as LP-90), and a lead has nested raw data.

nodes.name: Quarantine Row
nodes.notes:
Edge case 13, made concrete. The broken row is kept WITH its original text, so
the fix is: correct the cell, replay the dead letter through LP-05. Discarding
it and logging "1 row failed" would leave the operator with a number and no way
to act on it.

parameters.content:
## LP-01 Intake

Three sources in, one canonical lead out. `_shared/intake.js` holds every rule; the three `Normalize *` nodes only map field names, so there is no per-source logic downstream.

**Two keys, not one.** `idem_key` = *this delivery* (gated here). `person_key` = *this human* (resolved in LP-02, with a confidence score). Merging the two concepts breaks intake in both directions.

**Order matters:** claim -> store -> respond -> hand off. The response goes out before the processing, because WhatsApp retries anything it has not seen acknowledged for up to 7 days.

**A bad row never takes the batch down.** 50 rows, 1 broken: 49 imported, 1 dead letter with the original text attached, replayable through LP-05. (EC-13)
